title: Compiler diagnostics are structured only at the external CLI boundary
observed_need: Compile-fail and diagnostic tests must match diagnostic identity and preserve source spans without scraping human prose.
current_language_behavior: The Rust toolchain exposes versioned structured diagnostics and the native runner fail-closes on invalid admission. P-062 added a Test-owned MNCS application that projects diagnostic codes and applies compile verdict policy without building a host diagnostic-code list. P-063 replaces the application's Test JsonValue tree projection with bounded Stdlib JSON cursor events and retains only selected code strings; MNCS application code still cannot directly consume compiler Diagnostic values.
why_insufficient: The native projection removes duplicate host code extraction for supported documents, but Python still decodes the full diagnostics tree to preserve the public TestResult contract, and native diagnostic assertions still depend on the CLI JSON protocol.
minimal_reproducer: tests/fixtures/compile_fail.mncs plus tools/mncs_test.py: compile_entry retains detailed diagnostics for TestResult and sends the raw document to native/mncs/test/compile_diagnostic_verdict_v1.mncs for bounded code projection and verdict policy.
desired_direction: A versioned diagnostic value/protocol exposing code, severity, source span, related diagnostics, and rendered forms to native tooling.
workaround: The Test-owned native application scans up to 16,384 bytes with the Stdlib JSON cursor and syntax scanner, then retains at most 32 selected diagnostic code strings. Python continues decoding detailed diagnostics for public output and compatibility fallback; no formatted-stderr parsing is used.
